notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 74 this time, because the research tools stopped working before I could read a single source.

My first attempt to open the six main pages crashed. Those were Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes. The fix was ready, but when I tried again the tool said I had no requests left for this turn. So nothing came back from any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a link for each point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. With no pages read, I have nothing I can honestly put in a verse-by-verse note. Writing the commentary from memory and attaching links would break those rules and could misrepresent what those teachers wrote.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with:
- **The traditional reading:** Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Precept Austin.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Psalm 74, then Bible Odyssey. Likely topics are the dragons and Leviathan in vv. 13–14, which disaster the psalm describes, and the line "no longer any prophet" in v. 9.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** targeted searches on Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Spurgeon, the Wesley Center, LCMS and 1517, kept only where a source really takes a different view.
- **Catholic and Orthodox readings:** New Advent (where Augustine's commentary on the Psalms is likely to be), Catholic.com and OCA.
- **Debated popular teaching:** included only if a page on the approved sites actually discusses this psalm.
